# CRW-894 fix round 1: the findings of the independent verifier on 4636e20a (d1 link boundary and relative aliases, benign relative scripts, d3 json.tool shadowing).
# ../repo is the managed checkout.

=== CRW-894-vf-01 | U
--why python3 reads its program from the pipe through /proc/self/root/.. : the kernel follows the root link first, so the two dot-dot segments end at / and the path is /dev/stdin (verifier of 4636e20a, d1 link boundary).
printf 'import shutil; shutil.rmtree("../repo")\n' | python3 /proc/self/root/../../dev/stdin

=== CRW-894-vf-02 | U
--why python3 reads its program from the pipe through /proc/self/cwd/.. in the directory /: the cwd link is followed before the dot-dot segment.
cd /; printf 'import shutil; shutil.rmtree("../repo")\n' | python3 /proc/self/cwd/../dev/stdin

=== CRW-894-vf-03 | U
--why bash reads its script from the pipe through /proc/self/root/.. in front of /dev/stdin.
printf 'rm -rf ../repo\n' | bash /proc/self/root/../../dev/stdin

=== CRW-894-vf-04 | U
--why A bash input redirection through the root link and a dot-dot segment is the pipe.
printf 'rm -rf ../repo\n' | bash </proc/self/root/../dev/stdin

=== CRW-894-vf-05 | U
--why node reads its program from the pipe through the root link of pid 1 and dot-dot segments in front of /dev/fd/0.
printf 'import shutil; shutil.rmtree("../repo")\n' | node /proc/1/root/../../dev/fd/0

=== CRW-894-vf-06 | U
--why In a directory the reader does not know, dev/stdin is the stdin alias when the directory is /: the pipe is the program (verifier of 4636e20a, d1 unknown directory).
cd "$DIR"; printf 'import shutil; shutil.rmtree("../repo")\n' | python3 dev/stdin

=== CRW-894-vf-07 | U
--why In a directory the reader does not know, dev/fd/0 is the stdin alias when the directory is /: the pipe is the program (verifier of 4636e20a, d1 unknown directory).
cd "$DIR"; printf 'import shutil; shutil.rmtree("../repo")\n' | python3 dev/fd/0

=== CRW-894-vf-08 | U
--why In a directory the reader does not know, proc/self/fd/0 is the stdin alias when the directory is /: the pipe is the program (verifier of 4636e20a, d1 unknown directory).
cd "$DIR"; printf 'import shutil; shutil.rmtree("../repo")\n' | python3 proc/self/fd/0

=== CRW-894-vf-09 | U
--why In a directory the reader does not know, a lone descriptor number is the stdin alias when the directory is /dev/fd or /proc/self/fd: the pipe is the program (verifier of 4636e20a, d1 unknown directory).
cd "$DIR"; printf 'import shutil; shutil.rmtree("../repo")\n' | python3 0

=== CRW-894-vf-10 | U
--why In a directory the reader does not know, fd/0 is the stdin alias when the directory is /dev: the pipe is the program (verifier of 4636e20a, d1 unknown directory).
cd "$DIR"; printf 'import shutil; shutil.rmtree("../repo")\n' | python3 fd/0

=== CRW-894-vf-11 | U
--why In a directory the reader does not know, a dotted relative alias is the stdin alias when the directory is /: the pipe is the program (verifier of 4636e20a, d1 unknown directory).
cd "$DIR"; printf 'import shutil; shutil.rmtree("../repo")\n' | python3 ./dev/./stdin

=== CRW-894-vf-12 | U
--why In a directory the reader does not know, a dot-dot relative alias is the stdin alias from a directory two levels down: the pipe is the program (verifier of 4636e20a, d1 unknown directory).
cd "$DIR"; printf 'import shutil; shutil.rmtree("../repo")\n' | python3 ../../dev/stdin

=== CRW-894-vf-13 | U
--why In a directory the reader does not know, a relative alias through the root link is the stdin alias: the pipe is the program (verifier of 4636e20a, d1 unknown directory).
cd "$DIR"; printf 'import shutil; shutil.rmtree("../repo")\n' | python3 proc/self/root/../dev/stdin

=== CRW-894-vf-14 | U
--why In a directory the reader does not know, node reads its program from a relative stdin alias: the pipe is the program (verifier of 4636e20a, d1 unknown directory).
cd "$DIR"; printf 'import shutil; shutil.rmtree("../repo")\n' | node dev/stdin

=== CRW-894-vf-15 | U
--why In a directory the reader does not know, perl reads its program from a relative stdin alias: the pipe is the program (verifier of 4636e20a, d1 unknown directory).
cd "$DIR"; printf 'import shutil; shutil.rmtree("../repo")\n' | perl dev/stdin

=== CRW-894-vf-16 | U
--why In a directory the reader does not know, php reads its program from a relative stdin alias: the pipe is the program (verifier of 4636e20a, d1 unknown directory).
cd "$DIR"; printf 'import shutil; shutil.rmtree("../repo")\n' | php dev/stdin

=== CRW-894-vf-17 | U
--why In a directory the reader does not know, bash reads its script from the relative alias dev/stdin.
cd "$DIR"; printf 'rm -rf ../repo\n' | bash dev/stdin

=== CRW-894-vf-18 | U
--why In a directory the reader does not know, a bash input redirection from dev/fd/0 is the pipe.
cd "$DIR"; printf 'rm -rf ../repo\n' | bash <dev/fd/0

=== CRW-894-vf-19 | B
--why Control: a script in a sibling directory is no descriptor alias, so the interpreter is not judged (verifier of 4636e20a, benign accounting).
cd "$DIR"; printf x | python3 ../tools/gen.py

=== CRW-894-vf-20 | B
--why Control: a script below a directory named fd is no descriptor alias, so the interpreter is not judged (verifier of 4636e20a, benign accounting).
cd "$DIR"; printf x | python3 build/fd/gen.py

=== CRW-894-vf-21 | B
--why Control: a script in a directory named fd is no descriptor alias, so the interpreter is not judged (verifier of 4636e20a, benign accounting).
cd "$DIR"; printf x | python3 fd/gen.py

=== CRW-894-vf-22 | B
--why Control: a script whose name starts with stdin is no descriptor alias, so the interpreter is not judged (verifier of 4636e20a, benign accounting).
cd "$DIR"; printf x | python3 stdin_reader.py

=== CRW-894-vf-23 | B
--why Control: a script named stdin.py is no descriptor alias, so the interpreter is not judged (verifier of 4636e20a, benign accounting).
cd "$DIR"; printf x | python3 ../stdin.py

=== CRW-894-vf-24 | B
--why Control: a script whose name has fd and digits is no descriptor alias, so the interpreter is not judged (verifier of 4636e20a, benign accounting).
cd "$DIR"; printf x | python3 ./tools/fd10.py

=== CRW-894-vf-25 | B
--why Control: a node script in a parent directory is no descriptor alias, so the interpreter is not judged (verifier of 4636e20a, benign accounting).
cd "$DIR"; printf x | node ../tools/gen.js

=== CRW-894-vf-26 | U
--why python3 -m json.tool runs json/tool.py of the working directory when the directory holds a json package: the module is not the standard library (verifier of 4636e20a, d3).
--file json/__init__.py
import os
--file json/tool.py
print('local')
--cmd
printf x | python3 -m json.tool

=== CRW-894-vf-27 | U
--why A json.py in the working directory shadows the standard library json for python3 -m json.tool.
--file json.py
print('local')
--cmd
printf x | python3 -m json.tool

=== CRW-894-vf-31 | U
--why The json package shadow with the options of json.tool is still the local module.
--file json/__init__.py
import os
--file json/tool.py
print('local')
--cmd
printf x | python3 -m json.tool --sort-keys

=== CRW-894-vf-32 | U
--why The text creates the json package that python3 -m json.tool then runs.
mkdir json; printf 'print(1)' > json/__init__.py; printf x | python3 -m json.tool

=== CRW-894-vf-33 | U
--why The text copies a file to json.py that python3 -m json.tool then runs.
cp evil.py json.py; printf x | python3 -m json.tool

=== CRW-894-vf-34 | U
--why In a directory the reader does not know the module search path starts somewhere it cannot see: python3 -m json.tool is not proven.
cd "$DIR"; printf x | python3 -m json.tool
